THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County moved its 2027 budget toward final adoption and opened new ATV access on State Highway 34, while Wausau's economic development and waterworks boards wrestled with a funding shortfall for lead service line replacement and a deadlocked property decision headed to the full council.

  • Marathon County's Infrastructure Committee approved an ordinance allowing ATV/UTV access on State Highway 34 and directed staff to pursue flashing warning signs with the state DOT.
  • Wausau's Waterworks Commission flagged an estimated $2 million gap after a DNR lead service line funding award came in below expectations, with additional borrowing options headed to the finance committee.
  • Marathon County committees rejected all current proposals for a county building sale and directed staff to hire a real estate broker, while separately approving a one-year lease of the former UWSP theater to the Marathon Center for Arts and Culture — with the tenant covering roughly $7,428 in annual building insurance costs.
  • Wausau's Economic Development Committee approved buying a tax-delinquent property at 108 Myron Street for $1 to pursue affordable housing, pending county board sign-off November 10.
  • The Marathon County Environmental Resources Committee postponed a contested farmland-preservation-to-residential rezoning request in the Town of Marathon, citing neighbor opposition, to no earlier than January.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on its 2027 operating budget and related resolutions, and DC Everest's school board is set to review results from a recent community survey, both Monday evening.

Coming up: The Marathon County Board meets Tuesday, November 10 at 6 p.m. to adopt the 2027 budget and capital improvement plan — the most significant vote of the week. Wausau's Common Council also convenes Tuesday at 6:30 p.m., where the deadlocked Cleveland Avenue property matter is expected to land after the economic development committee's 2-2 tie.
